dedupe_keys.name: eu directive 2022 2557 on the resilience of critical entities cer directive and the commission list of essential services

description: The Directive on the Resilience of Critical Entities, Directive (EU) 2022/2557, is the European Union law that sets how member states identify and protect the operators of critical infrastructure. It entered into force on 16 January 2023 and member states had until 17 October 2024 to transpose it. Each state must adopt a national strategy and carry out regular risk assessments against natural hazards, terrorist attacks, insider threats, sabotage and public health emergencies, based on the list of essential services the Commission adopted for every covered sector, and must then identify critical entities, which run their own risk assessments, take resilience measures and notify incidents. Eleven sectors are covered: energy, transport, banking, financial market infrastructure, health, drinking water, wastewater, digital infrastructure, public administration, space and food. Entities serving six or more member states get extra advice, and a Critical Entities Resilience Group of national authorities chaired by the Commission shares practice. Format and access: the Commission policy page, updated January 2026, links the legal text, the work programme and contact lists. Licence: EU legal texts, free to reuse. Caveats: the page summarises the law and does not publish national lists of entities. It frames sector scope and hazard lists for resilience and hazard exposure models of European critical infrastructure. Related catalogue records are Ireland's transposing regulations and Slovakia's public list of critical entities.
